title: Q and W trim the clip under the playhead up to it, the Premiere way
goal: The quickest way to tighten a talking recording in Premiere is to park the playhead where the good part starts and press Q (ripple trim the start to here) or W (ripple trim the end to here). Here the same trim needs a cut, a click and a delete. Add Q and W on the timeline.
notes: Found by measure-the-video-editor-against-premiere-and-fi (2026-09-24); gap report docs/design/video-vs-premiere.md. Reproduced: q and w with the timeline focused are taken by nobody (five-minute walk log steps 23, 24). TimelineKeys.swift has no such command. Q is also Photoshop's quick mask, which the canvas does not use; confirm the canvas has no Q/W tool first. | Built 2026-09-24: PhotonzCore/RippleTrim.swift (rippleTrimClip, rippleTrimStretch, rippleTrim; reuses extractStretch so every unlocked track loses the stretch, markers and In/Out squeeze with the picture; marker move factored into moveMarkers in MarkedStretch.swift). TimelineKeys: .rippleTrimToPlayhead(.start/.end) on q/w when the timeline is focused, not on repeat. App: EditorState+TimelineMenus (rippleTrimToPlayhead, clip menu rows under Split at Playhead, enabled only on the piece holding the playhead), Video menu rows with Q/W printed only when the timeline has the keyboard. Tests: RippleTrimTests, TimelineKeysTests.qAndWTrim. Walks: ripple-trim-to-playhead-walk (lock-safe), ripple-trim-from-the-clip-menu-walk (right-click, needs an unlocked screen).
acceptance: Q removes everything from the start of the clip under the playhead up to the playhead and closes the gap, on every linked track
W removes everything from the playhead to the end of that clip and closes the gap
Both are one undo step and appear in the clip's right-click menu with their keys
A walk parks the playhead two seconds into a clip, presses Q, and the clip is two seconds shorter and starts where it did
Works at Next defaults with no switch turned on, and an audit written under queue/audits/ gives the try steps and a real picture
Anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar, and written into this task's log if it does not

log.note: adversarial pre-check: canvas has no Q tool; W is the Magic Wand on the canvas, so Q/W mean trim only while the timeline has the keyboard (same rule as I/O). Premiere's Q/W go to the previous/next edit on targeted tracks; here that is the piece under the playhead, which is what a screen recording has. Chose Extract semantics (every unlocked track loses the stretch) over ripple-delete semantics (music under it left alone) so a detached sound stays in sync, which is Premiere with sync lock on. A trim that would leave a sliver under 10ms is refused rather than silently taking the whole piece.

verified: RippleTrimTests + key tests green; Scripts/test.sh green on the second run (first run hit the known export-size flake, logged on its task). Both walks ok on the probe with real captures, screen unlocked, no flags. Audit queue/audits/2026-09-24-ripple-trim-to-playhead.json.

left rough, not filed: the clip right-click menu opens at the foot of the screen and scrolls after three rows (two more rows make it scroll sooner); the ruler-menu commit already noted this, and the user sees it in the audit capture. Menu rows act on the playhead's piece, so they go dim on other pieces: by design.
